questions.stem: Why have so few systemic drugs worked as pulmonary vasodilators?
questions.answer: Most pulmonary vascular receptors are not lung-specific, so side effects are unacceptable.

questions.stem: In lung disease, what does abolishing hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction remove?
questions.answer: The main compensation for poor gas exchange.

questions.stem: Why does inhaled nitric oxide not cause systemic vasodilation?
options: It is cleared by the kidneys
It is metabolised in the liver

questions.stem: How does inhaled nitric oxide improve oxygenation?
questions.answer: It diverts flow to well-ventilated lung, away from poorly ventilated lung.

questions.stem: With oxygen, how does the rate of nitric oxide oxidising to NO2 depend on NO concentration?
questions.answer: On the NO concentration squared, and on oxygen concentration.

questions.stem: Which lung harm does NO2 from inhaled nitric oxide cause?
Over time, what may happen to the benefit of inhaled nitric oxide?
What happens when inhaled nitric oxide is stopped abruptly?
options: Oxygenation rises and pulmonary artery pressure falls
Oxygenation falls and pulmonary artery pressure rises

questions.stem: In some acute lung injury patients, what does inhaled nitric oxide improve, and what does it not?
questions.answer: It improves oxygenation but not survival.

questions.stem: Why are adverse effects significant with IV prostacyclin in pulmonary hypertension?
Why are side effects of inhaled prostacyclin minimal, despite some systemic absorption?
What do phosphodiesterase inhibitors block in pulmonary artery smooth muscle?
By which routes are phosphodiesterase inhibitors used to lower pulmonary pressure?
Which phosphodiesterase type do sildenafil and tadalafil target in the pulmonary circulation?
When do ACE inhibitors lower pulmonary vascular resistance in pulmonary hypertension from lung disease?
How soon does losartan lower pulmonary artery pressure?
How do calcium channel blockers like nifedipine lower secondary pulmonary hypertension?
questions.answer: By blocking L-type calcium channels in pulmonary artery smooth muscle.

questions.stem: Why can calcium channel blockers worsen hypoxaemia in some patients?
What is the concern with high-dose calcium channel blockers in pulmonary hypertension?
questions.answer: They are negatively inotropic and can worsen right heart failure.

questions.stem: What do endothelin receptor antagonists do at ETA and ETB receptors?
In chronic hypoxia, endothelin contributes to what process that endothelin receptor antagonists may slow?
Which endothelin receptor antagonist is described as still in trials?
